summary: Out-route redirection causing long-tail inference latency and streaming timeouts for enterprise account
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden increase in tail latency and streaming timeouts starting ~2026-03-13 09:40 UTC. A subset of inference requests originating from Fillmore Health's US-west region are being routed through a remote eu-west hop, adding ~250-500ms extra handshake/TTFB and causing streaming sessions to frequently abort with 504/stream-cancel errors. Impact: elevated p95/p99 for both synchronous generation and streaming endpoints; several production user-facing failures.

Impact:
- Fillmore Health: ~20% of requests during window experienced >1s TTFB and 8% saw streaming disconnects/timeouts.
- Symptoms reported: increased p50->p99 gap, disconnected streams mid-response, client-side retries.

Environment:
- Prod (us-west-2) edge -> Redwood API -> serving runtime pool (dedicated capacity for customer).
- Customer is on enterprise tier with Dedicated capacity and geo-affinity pinned to us-west-2.

Observed behavior:
- Traces show unexpected next-hop: requests from edge proxy in us-west-2 are being forwarded to an intermediate egress proxy in eu-west-1 before reaching the serving runtime.
- TCP RTT for affected flows: ~120ms baseline vs ~420ms when redirected. TLS handshake durations correspondingly larger.
- Streaming protocol aborted at server-side with error: HTTP/1.1 504 Stream Timeout after prolonged TLS handshake.

Expected behavior:
- Requests should maintain local egress path to the serving runtime in us-west-2 with p50/p95 latency within expected SLOs.

Immediate mitigation performed so far:
- Support temporarily pinned customer route to local-pop via account routing tag which reduced affected fraction to <1% within 12 minutes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Fillmore Health API key and send continuous streaming generation requests to /v1/stream endpoint from client in us-west-2.
2) Observe p99 and streaming disconnect rate over 10-minute window.
3) Correlate traces (x-request-id) to edge logs and inspect next-hop egress proxy reported in X-Edge-Egress header.
4) Reproduce by forcing account to use global egress policy (simulated) to observe redirection behavior.
logs:
[2026-03-13T09:41:12Z] edge-proxy us-west-2 request_id=req-7a2f X-Edge-Egress: pop-eu-west-1-02; tls_handshake_ms=380; status=stream_cancel 504
[2026-03-13T09:41:13Z] serving-runtime us-west-2 request_id=req-7a2f accepted; kv_warm=false; recv_bytes=1024; process_ms=120
[2026-03-13T09:43:48Z] account-routing: Fillmore-acc (tag: enterprise-dedicated) -> routing-decider assigned egress pop-eu-west-1-02 due to transient route score flip
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-13T09:45:00Z: Customer reported ~30% of streaming sessions timed out. Collected sample request ids and escalated to SRE. Pinning customer to local-pop reduced errors during test window.

Connor Lee (SRE) 2026-03-13T10:02:00Z: Initial hypothesis: BGP community-based failover policy caused a temporary preference for eu-west egress for certain prefixes. Pulling network telemetry now. Not seeing capacity pressure on us-west serving pool.

Morgan Chen (Network) 2026-03-13T10:15:00Z: Confirmed transient route advertisement from a partner transit caused prefer-eu community to be attached; rolling back community filters for affected prefixes should stop redirects. Applying mitigation now.
Aisha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-13T10:28:00Z: Informed customer of temporary mitigation; monitoring for residual impact. Customer acknowledged and requested postmortem.
investigation_notes: Traces show consistent X-Edge-Egress header set to eu-west-1 for affected requests; correlation with netflow shows outbound AS path included partner-as-64521 during window.
No evidence of serving-runtime CPU/GPU saturation; KV cache warmup unaffected; increased latency coincides with extra cross-region hop and TLS handshake timeouts.
Routing-decider logs: recent weight recalculation at 2026-03-13T09:39:54Z applied transient penalty to us-west-2 due to a measured upstream health probe failure (false-positive) from partner network.
We observed higher connection churn on the partner peering session; partner has an upstream route flap which attached a prefer-eu community onto our prefixes for a short window.
resolution:
Mitigation: network team rolled back partner community filter and enforced local-pop preference for account routing tags. Support pinned Fillmore Health to their Dedicated us-west-2 pool until the routing-decider policy is updated.
Long-term fixes: 1) Update routing-decider to require multi-probe confirmation before applying inter-region penalties for prefixes with Dedicated affinity. 2) Add synthetic egress health probes to detect false-positive probe failures earlier. 3) Create automated rollback if cross-region egress rate for affinity-bound accounts exceeds threshold.
Customer communication: notified Fillmore Health about root cause and mitigations; provided timeline for permanent fix and agreed to formal postmortem.
